text.p: The Turkish lira closed easier at 88,835 to the dollar on Wednesday after 88,450 on Tuesday, in line with the dollar's gains against the mark.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory hard currency transfers at 88,600 lira, up from 88,275 at Tuesday's close.

Bankers said cash demand was strong as banks paid 69.6 trillion to the Treasury for Tuesday's 182-day t-bill auction in return for 57.7 trillion lira of maturing t-bills and central bank reverse repos.
To relieve the liquidity squeeze, the central bank injected 15.2 trillion lira by buying five-day repos from banks at an average annual rate of 72.84 percent on the open market.

It also funded 6.2 trillion lira overnight cash at 75 percent at the close of the interbank market as some banks were still short. Overnight rates moved between 69.25 and 73.5 percent during the day, ending at an average 73.81 percent, up from Tuesday's 71.57.

In the t-bill market, yields dropped between 1-3 points on higher-than-expected demand at Treasury's 182-day bill sale on Tuesday and on lower money rates, which briefly eased after the central bank's repo auction at midday.
The yield on the most active December 25 paper fell to 112.36 percent from 113.90 percent Tuesday average.
The second most heavily traded March 12, 1997 paper sold at an average 128.92 percent.
